transcript.text: Thanks for calling Summit Air, this is the virtual assistant. How can I help?
Hi, my carbon monoxide alarm is going off and it won't stop.
If a window is right there, open it. Then get everyone out of the house now and call 911 once you're outside.
Okay, I'm going outside now.
Good. Stay outside until the fire department says the house is safe. Once you're safe, can you tell me the address you're calling from? I'll get a person to follow up with you.
Okay. It's 31-18 30th Ave, Astoria, 11102. My name is Tomas Reyes.

Thanks, Tomas. Is the house clear and everyone outside now? Your address is in our service area. I've flagged this for a person, but I don't have a callback time to give you yet. Please keep everyone outside and wait for the fire department before going back in.
Okay, I'm outside now. Nobody else is home, it's just me. I have a little headache.

Tomas, a headache with a CO alarm going off means you need to get medical care now. Call 911 and tell them you have a headache and think there's carbon monoxide. Stay outside away from the house while you wait.
Okay, I'm going to call 911 now. Goodbye.
Good. Stay safe, Tomas. Goodbye. Please hang up now, get everyone outside, and call 911 from there. We'll follow up once you're safe.

transcript.text: Thanks for calling Summit Air, this is the virtual assistant. How can I help?
Hello, my heat isn't working and it's getting awfully cold in here.
Sorry to hear that. Since when has the heat been out?
Since last evening. The radiators went cold, and it's about fifty-five degrees in the apartment now.
Okay, fifty-five inside. What's the address, including the ZIP code?
It's 45 Forest Avenue, Staten Island, 10310.
You're in our service area. Is this your place, or are you renting?
It's my home. I've lived here a long time. I don't rent it from anyone.
Got it. Who's at home with you right now? Anyone who'd have a harder time with the cold?
It's just me. I'm eighty-four, and I live alone. I'm managing, but I'm cold, and I'd really appreciate someone coming out as soon as possible.
I'm sorry you're cold. Are you doing okay right now, and are you able to stay warm with blankets or by closing off the room you're in?

I'm all right for now. I've got a couple of blankets on me, and I'm sitting in the living room, which is the warmest room, so I'm keeping the door shut. It's not comfortable, though, and I don't want to sit like this all day.
Understood, and I'll get you in as soon as I can. What kind of heating system do you have, and roughly how old is it, if you know?
I think it's a boiler with radiators, though I'm not certain. It's been in the building for a long time, probably since before I moved in, so I couldn't tell you how old it is.
Thanks, that helps. Have you tried anything yet, like checking the thermostat or the boiler?
I checked the thermostat, and it's set up high, but nothing happens when I turn it. I haven't gone near the boiler. It's down in the basement, and with my cane I don't want to go down those stairs.
Good call staying off those stairs. Please don't try the basement. Anything else the technician should know when they get there, like a gate code, a buzzer or a dog?

There's a buzzer by the front door, and it says Marsh on it, so they can ring me up. No dog, and no gate code. The front door is unlocked during the day, so they can just come in if I don't answer right away, though I'd rather they ring first.
Okay, the buzzer says Marsh, and they'll ring first. What's the best phone number to reach you at? Is it the number you're calling from?
Yes, it's this number. It's a landline, and I'm usually right by the phone.
Because you're on your own and cold, I can get you in today. There's an opening this afternoon, 12 to 4. Would that work, or do you want tomorrow or Wednesday?
This afternoon, between 12 and 4, would be perfect. I'll take that window.
Before I book, I need to read back the details. Let me do that now. Let me read that back: 45 Forest Avenue, Staten Island, 10310, and the best number is 332, 555, 0118. Is that right?
Yes, that's right. The address and the number are both correct.
Can I get your name for the booking?
It's Evelyn Marsh. M-A-R-S-H.
You're all set for today, Monday, with the technician arriving between 12 and 4. They'll ring the Marsh buzzer first. Anything else?
No, that's everything. Thank you so much for getting someone out to me today. I appreciate it. Goodbye.
Glad we could get someone to you today. Stay warm, Ms. Marsh. Goodbye.

The final turn cost the most points, because it kept talking after Gloria said goodbye, read out internal steps ("I still need a callback time from the system… I'll try the flag again"), and said goodbye twice with an unclear "by 10 AM" callback; earlier turns also narrated slot picking aloud and asked two questions at once.

transcript.text: Hi, this is Summit Air. Is this Gloria?
Hi, it's Gloria. I'd like to schedule my yearly tune-up, and I'm a member so I should get priority scheduling, right?

Hi Gloria. I'm an AI assistant for Summit Air. I see your Summit Standard Membership ended on November 1st, so it's no longer active. I can have someone from the office call you about renewing it. For the tune-up, I can look at openings for you now. Is the address still 809 Union Street in Brooklyn?

Oh, no, my membership ended? I must have missed the renewal notice. Yes, I'm still at 809 Union Street in Brooklyn, 11206. And yes, please renew it for me. Can you check for a tune-up any weekday morning?

I can't renew the membership myself, but I'll take your request so someone from the office calls you about it. Let me check weekday mornings for the tune-up first. I have openings tomorrow, Tuesday the 3rd, Friday the 6th, and Monday the 9th, all in the morning. Which day works best for you?
Tuesday the 3rd works for me. Thank you.

Tuesday morning, between 8 and 12. Let me get the exact window for that day. Tuesday has 8 to 12 open, so I'll take that one. Before I book, I need a few details. What's the heating system's rough age, and is anything not working right now? You mentioned a yearly tune-up, so I'll note it as routine.
It's a furnace, and I think it's about twelve years old. It's been running fine, no strange noises or anything like that. It's just the yearly tune-up, like always.
Thanks. Earlier your file showed a Weil-McLain boiler from 2000, not a furnace. Is the system in your home a boiler, a furnace, or both?

Hmm, I don't think it's a boiler. We have forced air, with the vents in the floors and walls. I'm not sure what your file says, but that sounds like a mix-up with a different account. The unit in our basement is the furnace, and I'm fairly sure it's the one I had installed about twelve years ago.

Got it. I'll note that the furnace is about twelve years old and that the boiler on file may be wrong. Next, who's the best contact for the technician? And is there anything they should know when they arrive, like a gate code, a buzzer or a dog?

The best contact is me, Gloria Santos, at this number. There's no gate code. Ring the bell at the front door and I'll let them in. We don't have a dog, but my grandson sometimes visits, so please be patient if the bell takes a minute to answer. The furnace is in the basement, down the stairs just past the kitchen.

Noted. The tech will ring the front bell, and you'll be there. Now I'll read back the address and phone number before I book. Let me read that back: 809 Union Street, Brooklyn, 11206, and the best number is 929, 555, 0114. Is that right?
Yes, that's right. 809 Union Street, Brooklyn, 11206, and the number you're calling from is the best one to reach me. Thank you.
You're booked for tomorrow, Tuesday the 3rd, with the technician arriving between 8 and 12. They'll ring the front door bell, and I've noted the furnace in the basement. Anything else?
No, that's everything. Thank you so much for your help. And please have someone from the office call me about renewing the membership. Goodbye.

Sure. The membership renewal request is already logged, and someone from the office will call you about it. I need a callback time to give you, so I'll ask them to get in touch. Goodbye, Gloria. Stay warm out there. I still need a callback time from the system before I can confirm one. I'll try the flag again with a time. I've let the team know, and someone will call you by 10 AM about renewing your membership. Goodbye, Gloria. Stay warm out there.
